sources.entry: Write an OS in pure Rust

summary.title: Writing an OS in Rust
summary.one_liner: A multi-part blog tutorial series that builds a small x86_64 operating system kernel in Rust, with all code included in each post.
takeaways: How CPU exceptions are handled by setting up an interrupt descriptor table with handler functions
How to avoid fatal triple faults by handling double faults on a separate stack via an Interrupt Stack Table
How to configure the programmable interrupt controller and handle timer and keyboard hardware interrupts
How paging, virtual memory and multilevel page tables work on x86_64, and how to implement them in a kernel
How to implement heap allocators (bump, linked list, fixed-size block) and how async/await and a basic executor work in a kernel
summary.summary: This is a blog series in which each post is a small tutorial that extends a Rust operating system kernel step by step, with all needed code included. Topics covered run from CPU exceptions and double faults through hardware interrupts, paging, and heap allocation with several allocator designs, to cooperative multitasking with async/await and a basic executor. The page is the index for the second edition, which uses the bootloader crate; the first edition (built on GRUB) is still available but no longer updated. Source code is also in a corresponding GitHub repository.
